The U.S. legal hierarchy places the Constitution at the top as the supreme law of the land, followed by treaties and federal statutes that must not contradict it. Below these are administrative regulations issued by executive agencies, which derive their authority from enabling legislation in Congress or the President's powers under the Constitution. At the bottom level sit state laws and local ordinances, all of which remain subordinate to any conflicting higher-level provisions within this structure.
